audit.gl_error_proof: On each segment halfwidth h=1/16, Cauchy coefficients on radius R=1/8 bound Taylor tail after degree2q-1 by M*4^-q/(1-1/2). Both integral and positive Gaussian sum have mass2h, hence error<=8h*M*4^-q.40 segments give20*M*4^-q.
audit.theta_error_proof: For real t>=0, u=pi exp(2t)>3, K_j/K_1<=2*j^4*exp[-3(j²-1)].The sum j>=17 is at most4*17^4*exp[-3(17²-1)]<1e-300.Thus truncated kernel>= (1-1e-300) full kernel.
audit.tail_proof: For t>=5 the phase2n log t+9t/2-pi exp(2t) has derivative<=-pi exp(10), yielding tail<=64*pi²*5^(2n)*exp(45/2-pi exp10)/(pi exp10).This is for the raw moment, before division by(2n)!.
audit.phase_max_proof: For x in[-R,R], (x²+R²)^n exp(9x/2-alpha exp2x)<= (2R²)^n exp(9R/2).For x>=R, derivative2n*x/(x²+R²)+9/2-2alpha exp2x is strictly decreasing.The maximum is at R if its derivative is nonpositive there, or at its uniquely bracketed root.Upper phase uses bracket hi in positive terms and lo in the negative exponential.
audit.node_derivative_proof: |P_j|<=1 on[-1,1] from Laplace integral representation. P_n'=sum_{j<n,n-j odd}(2j+1)P_j implies |P_n'|<=n² and |P_n''|<=n^4. Apply midpoint derivative enclosure with root bracket radius2eps.
audit.external_reference: NIST DLMF3.5(v), equations3.5.18--3.5.21: Gaussian quadrature at orthogonal polynomial roots has positive weights and is exact through degree2q-1; Legendre normalization P_q(1)=1 has weights2/((1-x_i²)*P'_q(x_i)²).
